bib.title: Improving Multi-Task Deep Neural Networks via Knowledge Distillation for Natural Language Understanding

question: Can knowledge distillation from task-specific ensembles of MT-DNNs into one multi-task MT-DNN improve GLUE performance without increasing serving cost?
hypothesis: A single MT-DNN trained on the soft targets of ensemble teachers generalizes like the ensemble and beats a vanilla MT-DNN trained on hard labels, including on tasks without a teacher.
contributions: Extend Hinton et al. (2015) knowledge distillation to the multi-task learning setting of MT-DNN
New single-model GLUE state of the art of 83.7% (April 1, 2019 leaderboard)
Show gains also on tasks with no teacher, larger for tasks with less in-domain data

method.summary: Six MT-DNNs with varied shared-layer dropout are trained, the best 3 are fine-tuned per task (MNLI, QQP, RTE, QNLI) into 3-model ensemble teachers whose averaged class probabilities become soft targets. A student MT-DNN (same architecture as vanilla) is trained by multi-task learning with the per-task loss the average of hard-label and soft-target cross entropy, then fine-tuned per task.
method.task: multi-task natural language understanding (GLUE), knowledge distillation

datasets.name: GLUE (CoLA, SST-2, MNLI, RTE, WNLI, QQP, MRPC, STS-B, QNLI)
datasets.size: train: CoLA 8.5k, SST-2 67k, MNLI 393k, RTE 2.5k, WNLI 634, QQP 364k, MRPC 3.7k, STS-B 7k, QNLI 108k
datasets.split: dev/test per Table 1 (e.g. MNLI 20k dev, 20k test); test scored on GLUE server
datasets.preprocessing: wordpiece tokenization, spans no longer than 512 tokens; QNLI treated as two tasks (pairwise ranking on v1, classification on v2) with test results merged

models.name: MT-DNN_KD (student)
models.architecture: BERT-large shared layers (lexicon encoder + multi-layer bidirectional Transformer) with task-specific output layers

other.note: intro states BERT large has 24 transformer layers, 344 million parameters

models.name: MT-DNN ensemble teacher (per task: MNLI, QQP, RTE, QNLI)
models.init_from: Cased/Uncased BERT; shared layers from MT-DNN pretrained on GLUE via MTL; task output layers random

other.selection: 6 single MT-DNNs with shared-layer dropout in {0.1,0.2,0.3}; top 3 by MNLI and RTE dev

training.objective: Per task with teacher: average of cross entropy with hard labels (Eq 2) and cross entropy with soft targets Q = avg of K teacher class probabilities (Eq 3, 4); tasks without teacher use hard-label cross entropy. Mini-batches of single tasks, shuffled across tasks (Algorithm 1)

other.loss_weighting: equal-weight average; authors report no significant difference with other weights
other.teacher_dropout: shared-layer dropout in {0.1,0.2,0.3} for the 6 candidate models

inference.samples: not stated; no seeds or repeated runs reported

metrics.name: GLUE score
metrics.definition: overall benchmark score from GLUE server

eval.protocol: Test: GLUE leaderboard on April 1, 2019, single run; dev: Table 3. No seeds or significance test reported, though text says 'significantly'.

evidence.quote: A linear learning rate decay schedule with warm-up over 0.1 was used, unless stated otherwise.

results.claim: Distilled MT-DNN sets a new single-model GLUE test score
results.setup: GLUE test server, BERT-large based MT-DNN_KD, April 1 2019 leaderboard; baseline is vanilla MT-DNN
results.quote: creating a new state-of-the-art result of 83.7%

results.claim: Margin over second-best ALICE on the GLUE test set
Improvement over BERT_LARGE on GLUE test
MT-DNN_KD vs MT-DNN on RTE test
results.setup: GLUE test; RTE has teacher, 2.5k train examples

results.claim: MT-DNN_KD vs MT-DNN on CoLA test (no teacher)
results.setup: GLUE test; CoLA has no teacher, 8.5k train examples

results.claim: MT-DNN_KD vs MT-DNN on RTE dev
results.setup: GLUE dev, Table 3; MT-DNN-ensemble 86.7 (student exceeds its own teacher ensemble here)
results.note: Student 88.6 exceeds ensemble teacher 86.7 on RTE dev

results.claim: MT-DNN_KD vs MT-DNN on MRPC dev (no teacher), accuracy
MNLI-m dev: student vs ensemble teacher
results.setup: GLUE dev, Table 3; baseline_value is MT-DNN-ensemble; vanilla MT-DNN 87.1
results.note: Student keeps only part of the ensemble gap on MNLI (87.1 -> 87.3 vs ensemble 88.1)

results.claim: Student retains nearly all ensemble gain (qualitative)
results.setup: GLUE dev, Table 3, four teacher tasks and three no-teacher tasks

limits: Evaluated only on GLUE; teachers only for 4 of 9 tasks
No seeds, variance or significance tests despite 'significantly outperforms' wording
Dev improvement on larger tasks (MNLI, QQP) is small: 87.1 to 87.3, 91.9 to 91.9
Weight on hard vs soft loss not ablated in reported numbers; authors say no significant difference
Student cost, teacher training compute and hardware not reported
Comparison with ALICE and Snorkel MeTaL partly unclear (unpublished or ensemble); leaderboard claim dated April 1, 2019
Authors list future work: better combination of soft and hard targets, soft targets for unlabeled data, self-distillation
